fieldData.guide-section-heading: TikTok influencer marketing: a guide for brands
fieldData.guide-section-content:
What TikTok influencer marketing involves

TikTok influencer marketing means paying creators to feature your product in their TikTok videos. You choose the creators, agree the deliverables and the fee, review the video, then pay. A campaign can be one video from one creator or an ongoing partnership with many.

TikTok creators on Jem Social

As of November 17, 2026, Jem Social lists 951,642 US TikTok creators with 5,000 or more followers. This table splits them by follower count and shows how many list engagement of 3% to 20% and of 6% to 20%.

Most TikTok creators are small: 87% have fewer than 100,000 followers. Listed engagement doesn't fall as accounts get bigger in this data. In each follower range, 54% to 62% of creators list 6% to 20% and 75% to 83% list 3% to 20%. So compare a creator with others in the same range, and watch their recent videos, instead of relying on one number.

Counts are estimates from Jem Social's search and change between pulls. Engagement is the rate listed in Jem Social, with anything above 20% left out as a likely data error. Tools calculate engagement differently, so don't compare these figures with numbers from other sources. See the top 20 by engagement on the TikTok influencers list.

Looking for a TikTok influencer agency? An agency makes sense if you want someone else to run the whole campaign. If you'd rather pick the creators yourself, a platform handles the search, outreach and payment.

See how Jem Social's price compares with 7 other platforms.

How to choose TikTok creators

  • Engagement rate for their size. Compare creators in the same follower range, not against the whole market. The Engagement Rate Calculator works it out from any public profile.
  • Views against followers. Check how many views their recent videos get compared with how many followers they have.
  • Audience. Check where a creator's followers live and how old they are, so their audience matches your buyers. Jem Social shows audience data on each profile.
  • Recent content. Watch their latest videos and past brand deals. Is it the quality you'd run in your own ads?
  • Niche fit. A creator whose followers already care about your category needs less explaining.
  • A real following. Look for steady follower growth, comments from real people, and videos that match what the creator says they do.

What TikTok creators cost

Rates depend on followers, deliverables (how many videos, and how long) and usage rights, so there's no single price. The Influencer Rate Calculator covers TikTok and gives a starting point, and each creator's rate estimate is in Jem Social. Agree on deliverables and usage rights before any content is made.

Disclosure, usage rights and Spark Ads

The FTC says an endorsement should make it obvious when the creator has a relationship with the brand. The disclosure should sit with the endorsement itself, not only on a profile page or behind a "more" link, and for a video it should be in the video, not only the description. (FTC: Disclosures 101 for Social Media Influencers, checked November 17, 2026.)

TikTok says creators must turn on the commercial content disclosure setting when they post content that promotes a brand, product or service. (TikTok Ads Help Center, checked November 17, 2026.)

If you want to run a creator's video as an ad, Spark Ads use the creator's own post with their authorization. Creators can authorize it by generating a code in the video's ad settings. (TikTok Ads Help Center, checked November 17, 2026.) Agree this before the video is made.

TikTok also says it doesn't allow paid political advertising, including creators being compensated for making branded political content. (TikTok Ads Help Center, checked November 17, 2026.) See our guide to working with conservative creators for what that means in practice.

Put these in your brief: ask creators to turn on the disclosure setting and say it in the video, and say up front whether you'll want to run the video as an ad. This is general information, not legal advice.

Running your first TikTok campaign

  1. Write a brief: the product, deliverables (how many videos and how long), talking points, budget and deadline. The Campaign Brief Generator gives you a template.
  2. Shortlist TikTok creators in Jem Social and message them.
  3. Agree on rates, deliverables, usage rights and the disclosure setting.
  4. Review the video. Payment is released once you approve it.
  5. Measure the results with the Influencer Marketing ROI Calculator.

Hiring on more than one platform? See the Instagram influencer marketing guide.

fieldData.why-section-heading: Why TikTok influencer marketing outperforms reach-based buying.
fieldData.why-section-description: TikTok campaigns work best when brands prioritize fit over follower count. Vetted creators with strong engagement, audience quality, and content authority drive better outcomes than buying reach alone and Jem Social helps brands find them faster.
fieldData.why-card-1-description: TikTok creators often build stronger audience relationships because their content feels native to TikTok and specific to the communities they serve.
fieldData.why-card-2-description: Most partnerships with TikTok creators are easier to test than large national campaigns, making them useful for controlled brand experiments.
fieldData.why-card-3-description: TikTok creators can help brands reach buyers through trusted recommendations and the engaged communities they've built on TikTok.
fieldData.why-card-4-description: From outreach to published content, TikTok campaigns can move quickly when the brief and offer are clear.
